Subject: Weekly Fleet & Pipeline Convergence — agenda + ask (Nimbus focus)

Team — kicking off this week's convergence for deals where dedicated sizing interacts with fleet planning. Nimbus is the lead ask this week; attached is their updated forecast (Nimbus_Monthly_Forecast_Q4.xlsx). Key items for today's sync: 

- Confirm committed slot estimate for Nimbus pilot (they're asking to double burst in M2).
- Determine shortfall vs. current reserved pools and plan burst credit use.
- Decide whether to trigger a 2-week hardware hold request to Infra for extra nodes (Marissa input).
- Identify finance constraints for any one-time credits or accelerated procurement (Ben).

Please review the attached workbook before 11:30 PT and reply with any hard constraints. If you have updated usage profiles (p50/p95 seq lengths, embeddings vs. gen split), paste them inline.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov

Thanks, Olga. Quick notes after scanning their workbook and following up with Ari: 

- Nimbus pilot (POC) wants a steady 80 reserved slots for the first month, then scale to 160 as they hit their internal MLP. They also request the ability to burst to 240 for short stress tests (2–4 hour windows).
- Workload mix: 60% generation (avg seq 512, p95 1024), 30% embeddings, 10% rerank. Peak token cadence concentrated 10:00–14:00 PT.
- Proposed Redwood ask: reserve 120 slots to start (tradeoff on cost vs. lead risk).

Questions for Infra: can we support 240 bursts with current pool fragmentation? If not, what's minimum lead time for a temporary node add?

Karthik

Hi Karthik / Olga — confirming the numbers above from our side. A couple of clarifications: 

- The 240-burst is occasional (we expect 2–3 times in the first 30 days) but critical for our internal load tests.
- We can accept a staged start at 120 reserved with an SLA-backed ramp to 160 within 30 days if Redwood commits to the ramp schedule.
- For the SOC2/evidence asks the procurement team will also need a concise list of logs/controls — we attached an initial questionnaire request (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf) to this thread.

Happy to join the call if that helps.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet & Pipeline Convergence — agenda + ask (Nimbus focus)

Looping infra constraints in-line. TL;DR: short bursts to 240 are possible only if we consolidate fragmentation or provision ephemeral nodes; lead time varies by supplier. Details: 

- Current reserved pools: 480 slots across region; fragmentation across AZs reduces contiguous availability for 240-burst to ~160 without rebalancing.
- Option A (fast): ephemeral AWS/EPC nodes — ~48–72 hour lead time to fully provision and test; cost: premium hourly + network overhead.
- Option B (medium): migrate low-utilization pools into Nimbus bucket (requires migrations window, ~5 days) — risk to other deals during migration.
- Option C (slow): schedule next hardware procurement cycle (6–8 weeks).

Immediate ask from Infra: give us a decision on preferred option by EOD so we can start procurement or scheduling. Also attaching short runbook in Drive (link in thread).

— Marissa
Director, Infrastructure Operations
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet & Pipeline Convergence — agenda + ask (Nimbus focus)

Finance view: we can support a one-off credit to offset premium ephemeral node hours for the first month if sales commits to a >12 month reserve (simple payback model in brief below). Items to approve today: 

- One-time credit cap: $45k for ephemeral node usage (covers 72 hrs * premium rate + buffer).
- Reserve commit ask: 12-month minimum, minimum committed spend $1.2M.
- If we migrate pools (Option B), we need a mitigation plan for any deals affected; that's a separate finance risk but likely manageable with ~10% contingency holdback.

If we proceed with Option A, finance needs an expected ephemeral hour estimate by 17:00 PT to finalize the credit cap.

Ben
Head of Finance Operations

Thanks all — summary and action register below. Please treat deadlines as firm so we can give Nimbus a definitive ramp plan tomorrow morning.

Summary: 
- Start point: Redwood proposes 120 reserved slots for Nimbus day-1 with a committed ramp to 160 within 30 days (per Karthik / Ari).
- Burst: allow ephemeral bursts to 240 for up to 3 windows in month-1 (Marissa to confirm provisioning path).
- Finance: Ben pre-approves a $45k cap for ephemeral use pending exact hour estimate; sales to provide hours by 17:00 PT.
- SOC2: Karthik to coordinate with Nimbus on the evidence list; Laura will own the procurement checklist.

Action items (owners / due):
- Karthik: send Nimbus expected ephemeral hr estimate and confirm 12-month commitment cadence with customer (due 2026-12-01 17:00 PT).
- Marissa: confirm whether Option A or B (ephemeral vs. migration) and provide provisioning ETA (due 2026-12-02 12:00 PT).
- Ben: finalize credit cap paperwork if ephemeral hours estimate falls within projection (due 2026-12-02 15:00 PT).
- Laura: prep procurement + SOC2 response checklist and start the DocuSign for the ramp clause (due 2026-12-03 10:00 PT).

I'll consolidate final plan and send to Nimbus tomorrow 09:00 PT. Ari — thanks for the quick turnaround on the questionnaire; we'll loop back on specifics in the DocuSign and the next call.

Olga
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
